key_insight: RECAST shifts retrieval from simply finding relevant text to computing the right context when the answer must be derived across multiple sources. It learns to route evidence through adaptive filtering, aggregation, and computation instead of relying only on similarity search.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the limitation of standard RAG and retrieval-centric agents: many real-world tasks require synthesized evidence that is not explicitly contained in any single document chunk. This makes fixed top-k retrieval insufficient for complex, long-context reasoning over heterogeneous sources.
method: Learn an adaptive evidence-routing policy that decides how to transform and combine retrieved information.
Route evidence through operations such as filtering, aggregation, and computation to build the needed context.
Replace purely similarity-based retrieval with a more task-aware process for assembling answer-supporting evidence.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this means more reliable performance on tasks where the answer must be derived rather than directly retrieved. It can improve long-context QA, multi-document reasoning, and agent systems that must work with messy, distributed information.

paper_title: RECAST: Learning to Compute the Right Context through Adaptive Evidence Routing
paper_authors: Yilun Hao, Krishna Sayana, Isabella Ye, James S Ren, Sukhdeep Sodhi
